newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity closes lower, supply seen higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity closes lower, supply seen higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures closed lower amid expectations that several thousand megawatts of idled generation will come back on line over the next week or so, market sources said Wednesday.
"Everybody is trying to figure out what that means for the market. People are thinking that (futures prices) look kind of heavy," said one trader.
Sources noted prices ran up sharply Tuesday amid news of an unplanned outage at the 1,221 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Palo Verde nuclear power plant in Arizona.
But the unit looks likely to restart late Wednesday, easing concerns of a prolonged outage, sources said.

The market was also little concerned about a delay until this weekend of plans to restart the 1,087 MW unit 1 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear plant in central California, which has been shut for refueling since mid-April.
Instead, focus was on the approximately 3,000 MW of coal-fired generation scheduled to return to the market through next week as scheduled spring maintenance outages are completed.
Traders also cited weaker natural gas prices as contributing to the weaker tone in the power futures complex.
The June NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas contract closed down 1.7 cents at $2.346 per million British thermal units.
July Palo Verde (PV) electricity settled 91 cents lower at $30.31 per megawatt hour (MWH), compared with a high for the day of $30.95.
August PV lost 77 cents to close at $31.70, while September fell 57 cents to end at $28.79.
July California Oregon Border (COB) closed down 42 cents at $22.69, after trading as high as $23.35 and as low as $22.25.
August COB settled 92 cents lower at $25.53, while Septemberfell 40 cents to $24.50.
Trade volumes were not immediately available from NYMEX.
A total of about 7,000 megawatts of power generation, including the two nuclear units, remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance.

In addition to the Palo Verde and Diablo Canyon nukes, the following coal plants: a 750 MW unit at Colstrip in Montana, a 750 MW unit at Four Corners in Arizona, a 550 MW unit at Jim Bridger in Wyoming and a 400 MW unit at Bonanza plant in Utah, were scheduled to return to service by Monday.

In a six to 10-day outlook released Wednesday, the National Weather Service forecast above normal temperatures for California, Nevada, southern portions of Oregon, southwestern Idaho, western and central Utah and the western third of Arizona.
